title: Campaign Approval v1
description: Machine-readable schema for the parsed data model of a Two-Lane v1 campaign approval document (docs/experiments/schemas/two-lane-v1/campaign-approval.schema.md). Two explicit, discriminated profiles: 'example' (documentation/template, always non-operative -- carries the marker field, and permits documented placeholder string values such as '<HUMAN-FILLS-IN ...>') and 'operative' (omits marker entirely, and enforces strict field formats). oneOf is used so a document matches exactly one profile, never both, and never neither.
$comment: The two branches below are DELIBERATELY fully independent field definitions -- they do not share a single set of field schemas via a common allOf reference. An earlier revision of this schema referenced one shared 'commonFields' definition (with strict RFC3339/sha256-hex patterns) from BOTH branches; because allOf constituents are evaluated independently and ALL must pass, that shared reference silently forced the STRICT operative-grade patterns onto the example/template branch too, which made the documented blank template (whose approved_at is the literal placeholder string '<HUMAN-FILLS-IN RFC3339 timestamp>') fail its own documentation schema. Each branch below now defines its own fields from scratch: the example/template branch is permissive (any non-empty string is accepted for fields a human has not filled in yet), and the operative branch alone carries the strict patterns.

oneOf.title: example-or-template profile (always non-operative; permits documented placeholder values)
operative profile (must omit marker entirely; strict field formats)
